title: Validate connected periodic cut graphs through checker material and bake hookup

workflow: connected periodic compound hard-surface or tubular form

preconditions: the low cage is independently authored and connected where the form is continuous
high and low are in separate collections
action_policy: Identify periodic tube-like regions and open them with a concealed longitudinal seam rather than accepting a UV layer by itself.
Normalize layout scale, arrange the cut surface with positive margin, run a geometric collision audit, and render a checker on the actual material.

For tangent normal baking, make the low material's target Image Texture active, use Cycles selected-to-active, set positive margin, save the image, use Non-Color, and connect through a Normal Map node.
Reject a visually self-intersecting or badly distorted cage even when structural checks pass.
failure_predicates: no longitudinal cut on a periodic surface
checker stretch beyond the declared limit
bake image not saved or node not connected
recovery: move or add seams at hidden structural boundaries
straighten an orthogonal active quad before Follow Active Quads
pin stable regions and relax locally
reduce bend radius or improve cage geometry before blaming the unwrap
reselect the correct bake target node and rebake

sources.description: CG Boost demonstrates seams, Live Unwrap, stretch display, Follow Active Quads, packing, compound-form decomposition, and focal texel allocation.
Ryan King Art demonstrates active image targets, overlap repair, Cycles baking, margin, color-space choice, saving, and PBR node hookup.
Blender's current manual constrains UV texture use and image-bake prerequisites.

experiments.counterevidence: Checker stretch remains visible on tight curvature; one seam materially improves these forms but is not a universal distortion cure.

version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS reproduction; tutorial UI spans Blender 4.x-era workflows
